benchmark_kind: multi-axis scalability and efficiency measurement of the EXPERIMENTAL relation-paged backend
protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties, preprocessing included
scope_warning: Synthetic fixtures on a single host, 100-800 entities, 2-4 owners, 1-8 queries. All three parties ran on one machine, which does not instantiate the non-collusion assumption. No real dataset, no WAN, no multi-host run. Both protocols involved are passive; nothing here is a malicious-security result.
question: relation_paged_scaling.json varied entity count alone. The analytic cost model claims cost is Theta((1 + frontier_slots) * (entities*relations*owners + pool)). This benchmark moves every factor in that expression independently, and validates the model on axes it was not fitted to.

scaling_law_per_axis.method: log-log slope between the endpoints of each axis; 'net of floor' subtracts the ~130 MB size-independent term first, which is the honest exponent for the growing part

graph_size_directory_rows.verdict: linear in entities*relations; the sub-1 raw exponent is the fixed floor diluting a 7.9x range

federation_size_owners.verdict: SUPERLINEAR, approaching quadratic. Per-address work is proportional to owners AND the dependent address count is 1 + owners*frontier_per_owner, also proportional to owners. This is the worst axis in the system, and it is the axis that makes the system federated.

batch_size_queries.verdict: exactly linear. Batching provides NO amortization; 8 queries cost 7.96x one query. This is a controlled confirmation of the cross-fixture observation in relation_paged_scaling.json.

relation_count.verdict: linear in relations, as directory rows = entities * relations

per_key_degree.verdict: superlinear. Degree sets frontier width, which multiplies the dependent-read count, and also drives a compaction term quadratic in degree.

dominant_coefficient.stability: 0.0305 +/- 0.0001 across four independent fits with different feature sets and training splits; this is the one coefficient that is well identified

cost_model_validation.known_residual_structure: The worst held-out point is per-key-degree 4 at -12.4%, underpredicted. The fitted model omits compaction_selection_cells = queries * owners * slots_per_key * frontier_per_owner, which is quadratic in per-key degree. Adding it would overparameterize a 15-point dataset, so it is documented rather than fitted.
cost_model_validation.identifiability_caveat: The unpacks and topk_visits coefficients are collinear (both proportional to frontier_slots * second_width) and are individually meaningless; the negative topk coefficient is compensating for the inflated unpacks coefficient. Only their combination predicts, and only the products coefficient is interpretable.
cost_model_validation.methodological_note: An earlier two-term fit on entities+owners alone achieved 0.3% error and looked conclusive. It was wrong: held out against the query-count axis it underpredicted by up to 17%, because neither training axis varied the query count. Single-axis validation of a multi-axis cost model is not validation.

obliviousness_overhead.definition: total secure products divided by the number of values actually needed to answer the query
obliviousness_overhead.measured_on: entities=200, relations=8, owners=2 and owners=4 (identical, as expected: the ratio is a property of the layout, not the federation size)
obliviousness_overhead.reading: This is not waste to be optimized away; it IS the hiding. Touching every row is what makes the access pattern independent of the secret address, and it is why there is no volume or access-pattern leakage to attack.

stage_profile_percent_of_protocol_time.reading: The dependent second hop plus top-k is 82.2% of protocol time. Optimization effort anywhere else is capped at 18%.

layout_choice_matters.span: 3.07x between best and worst (page_size, pages_per_key) pair at equal semantics
layout_choice_matters.rule: set page_size to the maximum (source, relation) degree with pages_per_key = 1 when degree is uniform; the shipped fixture choice (page_size 2, pages_per_key 1) is uniquely optimal under a realistic page budget
layout_choice_matters.caveat: computed from the analytic model with page_budget recomputed per page_size from the actual data. Holding page_budget fixed flatters large pages and inverts part of the ranking.

what_this_does_not_show: Any real-dataset, WAN, or multi-host result.
Any measurement above 800 entities, 4 owners, or 8 queries.
That the cost model extrapolates beyond the measured ranges; held-out error is 5.25% mean within them and is not a guarantee outside them.
A fitted compaction term; its omission is the known residual and is documented, not corrected.
